root_idea.summary: The root centers on raising or proclaiming a voice, and extends by association to things marked by that proclamation or resembling the crescent seen at its announcement.
root_idea.development: The principal development runs from vocal proclamation—especially the pilgrimage talbiyah or a declaration—to the new moon, named in connection with people raising their voices upon seeing it. Further extensions include crescent-shaped objects, gleaming forms, and related expressions of sound.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Distinct Quran-attested Form IV verb group; the public headword is normalized to the active perfect citation form.
Distinct Quran-attested nominal group, presented under its supported singular citation form.

senses.definition: To pronounce a name over an offering; in the Quranic passive construction, to have an animal consecrated by invoking the name of one other than Allah.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form is passive, أُهِلَّ بِهِ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ, and refers to an animal slaughtered or dedicated with a name other than Allah's.

quranic_forms.public_pos_label: Noun · plural form in the Quran

senses.definition: A new moon: the moon in its early visible phase, especially the first part of the lunar month.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic plural أَهِلَّة in 2:189 refers to recurring new-moon phases as time markers for people and for pilgrimage. The exact early boundary is described variously in the lexical evidence, but the common focus is the moon near its beginning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A crescent-shaped, curved, or similarly named object: a two-pronged spearhead, a kind of snake, a snake's sloughed skin, a small rounded quantity of water at the bottom of a well, the broken end of a millstone, or the part joining the two bends of a pack saddle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are established extended uses associated with the form or resemblance of the crescent, rather than the astronomical meaning.
The term is explained as an extension associated with the sound of water in vigorous flow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To raise the voice, proclaim aloud, or make a sound; specifically, to recite the pilgrimage talbiyah aloud or to proclaim a declaration such as “There is no god but Allah.”
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: الإهلال may refer to raising the voice upon seeing the new moon and is also used more generally for producing a sound; أَهَلَّ بِالْحَجِّ denotes vocal proclamation of the pilgrimage formula.
Used of a newborn who begins life by crying aloud.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek sight of the new moon.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the sight-seeking use associated with the beginning of the lunar month.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the new moon to appear or be seen.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the construction أَهَلَّ الْهِلالُ, referring to the moon's becoming visible.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a cloud to gleam or glitter with lightning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use based on the visual resemblance of the flash to the crescent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Loosely or sparsely woven, of a garment or cloth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive adjective for fabric of flimsy or open weave.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Thin, attenuated, or lightly composed, especially of poetry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective is also used in the traditional epithet مُهَلْهِل for a poet associated with making verse less dense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To call out repeatedly while pursuing someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of repeated shouting in an attempt to overtake or reach a pursued person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw back or lose courage after charging an opponent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The idiom describes one who attacks an adversary and then retreats or holds back.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A call addressed to horses, meaning “feed” or “eat.”
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional vocal command directed at horses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The first night of a lunar month.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression مُسْتَهَلُّ الشَّهْرِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An interrogative particle used to ask a question and, in rhetorical contexts, to prompt recognition, rebuke, or an implied negation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a grammatical particle discussed alongside the root's homographic material; it is not one of the two supplied QAC form groups.

cautions: The public verb headword أَهَلَّ is the normalized active citation form, while all four supplied Quran occurrences are passive أُهِلَّ.

The boundary of هِلَال is described variously as the first two or first few nights, or more generally the interval near conjunction; the Quranic definition therefore uses the broader early-visible-phase wording.
هَلْ is retained as a separately headed grammatical item because it is explicitly discussed in the supplied lexical evidence, although no corresponding QAC form group is present.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The unexplained poetic phrase containing يَهِلُّ وَيَنْقَعُ in the root discussion does not provide enough context to assign a distinct lexical meaning confidently.
